title: Pommes Anna
description: A classic French potato dish featuring wafer-thin potato slices layered with clarified butter, thyme, and seasoning, baked until golden and crispy.
steps: Clarify the butter by melting it and skimming off the milk solids until only pure butter fat remains.
Slice the potatoes wafer-thin (about 1mm) using a mandolin. Do not wash the slices.
Prepare the pan by brushing the base with clarified butter.
Arrange the first layer of potatoes in a pretty flower or spiral shape, overlapping by about a centimeter.
Build the layers by repeating the process: butter, salt, thyme, pepper, and potato slices. Season every three layers.
Finish with a generous layer of butter on top, cover with a cartouche (baking paper circle), and place a weight on top.
Bake at 165°C for about an hour until a knife glides through with no resistance.
Increase the oven temperature to 220°C and bake for another 20 minutes to crisp up the exterior.
Turn the potato cake out onto a plate, brush with remaining butter, and finish with flaky salt and fresh

healthy: Potatoes give potassium and some fiber.
not_healthy: Clarified butter adds a lot of saturated fat.
